evidence.command_or_count: 192 live requests (bound 200), 0 failures, clamp_stats={clamped:0,max_overrun:0}; kill median retention of naive_mutable after turn 2 = 1.0 > 0.50
evidence.lock: flock(LOCK_EX) on .occamy.lock held for the whole batch; waited 0.0 s

finding.headline: Moving volatile values from the append-only delta into the mutable system/header block destroys prefix reuse: naive_mutable holds a flat ~800-token floor (10.1-10.4% of the final prompt) while pointer/naive_append reach 93.3-94.2% at turn 16.
finding.mechanism: naive_mutable rewrites message 0 every turn, so the served prefix breaks at the header. The ~768/832-token plateau is the surviving constant floor (64-token grid) of the unchanged remainder of the header, not the conversation history.
finding.after_turn2_note: The 1.0 is a self-normalisation artefact: naive_mutable's cached_max IS its floor, so retention pins at 1.0 by construction. On the absolute scale the ordering inverts.

kill_condition_evaluation: Pre-registered test applied literally: median retention of naive_mutable over turns>=3 is 1.0, which is > 0.50, so the volatility claim is reported REFUTED as instructed. CAVEAT recorded, not used to overturn the verdict: the statistic is degenerate for this arm because cached_max(naive_mutable) is the ~800-token floor, so any constant-cached arm scores 1.0. The absolute measurements in the same deliverable contradict a 'no penalty' reading.
assumptions: Turns per scenario = 16, not the full 48: 3 arms x 4 scenarios x 48 turns = 576 live requests, 2.9x the 200 hard bound. 16 is the largest depth covering 4 of the 6 registered depths (2/4/8/16) inside the bound (192). Depths 32 and 48 are the named remainder.
'After turn 2' read as turn >= 3; statistic = median across all arm x scenario x turn cells.

Volatile values are generated deterministically from sha256(scenario:turn:seed=1729) rather than a wall clock, so a rerun renders identical bytes; all four fields (ts, counter, run_id, tool_calls) change every turn.

pointer and naive_append share the SAME salt tag (accounting for their being equal-information); naive_mutable gets its own. Radix crossing is prevented structurally by running arms as separate passes. Without this the recipe control could not be byte-identical.

Server-side prefix cache was used as configured; no cache flush was requested (not ours to toggle). Each arm was a single serial pass so ordering effects are disclosed by the naive_append reproduction.
max_tokens=8, thinking=false, temperature=0.0 — the completion length is irrelevant to cache accounting.
next_unit_hint: The kill statistic is degenerate for any constant-cached arm: prefer an ABSOLUTE measure (cached_tokens/prompt_tokens at a fixed turn) before re-running a kill test of this shape. If depths 32/48 matter, re-run only naive_mutable (4 scenarios x 16 extra turns = 64 requests) against the existing pointer rows in rows.jsonl; a fresh verifier should re-read rows.jsonl and recompute the medians independently.
